name: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning with Reasoning
authors: Eric Zelikman*, Yuhuai Wu* (Stanford + Google Research), Jesse Mu, Noah D. Goodman; lead affiliation Stanford University Department of Computer Science (Zelikman and Wu contributed equally).
venue: NeurIPS 2022 (36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems); also arXiv preprint 2203.14465. Semantic Scholar CorpusID:247762790.
code_url: https://github.com/ezelikman/STaR (official code release stated in the NeurIPS camera-ready).
reflection_type: learned-critic-model is NOT used; the closest fit is a self-improvement training loop with an answer-conditioned 'rationalization' repair step. There is no verbal in-context self-critique at inference. The corrective signal is a ground-truth-answer-checked filter plus a backward 'reason-from-the-answer' (rationalization) generation step, distilled into weights via SFT. Best categorized as: outcome-verified self-training with answer-hinted rationalization (not verbal-self-critique, not multi-agent-debate).
feedback_source: ground-truth-oracle. The improvement signal is the binary correctness of the model's final answer checked against the dataset's ground-truth label (indicator reward 1(y_hat = y)). Correct-answer rationales are kept; for problems answered wrong, the correct answer is fed back as a hint to generate a rationalized rationale. No external tool/compiler, no unit tests, no human-in-the-loop, no learned reward model.
iteration_structure: population/evolutionary is NOT it; it is an iterative bootstrapping outer loop (expert-iteration style): each outer iteration (1) generates rationales for the whole training set with the current model, (2) filters by answer correctness (+ rationalization on failures), (3) fine-tunes a FRESH copy of the original pre-trained model on the accumulated correct rationales, then repeats. Crucially each iteration RE-TRAINS from the original pretrained checkpoint rather than continuing the previous checkpoint. Runs up to ~36 iterations (arithmetic ~20; GSM8K capped at the 30th iteration / 7912 steps).
reflection_object: model weights (primary). STaR modifies the model's parameters via SFT on self-generated reasoning chains; the artifact being improved is the policy that produces reasoning chains. Secondarily the unit being generated/curated is the reasoning chain (rationale/scratchpad), and the rationalization step reflects on a failed answer by reasoning backward from the correct answer. It does NOT modify prompts, action trajectories, or maintain an episodic memory store.
learning_locus: gradient_weight_update. STaR's improvement is realized entirely through fine-tuning (gradient updates) on filtered self-generated rationales; there is no in-context-only / test-time-only mechanism. The authors frame the loop as approximating an RL-style policy-gradient objective implemented with standard LLM training machinery.
requires_training: SFT (supervised fine-tuning) on filtered self-generated rationales, applied iteratively. The authors note STaR can be viewed as approximating an RL policy-gradient objective (with greedy decoding to reduce variance and multiple gradient steps per batch, akin to PPO-style reuse), and rationalization as an off-policy estimate of that objective, but the concrete implementation is iterated supervised fine-tuning, not an explicit PPO/DPO/RL optimizer. Optimizer: Adam, learning rate 1e-6 (searched 1e-7 to 1e-4), batch size 8 x length 1024, on a single TPU-v3 node.
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward (binary answer-correctness against ground-truth labels) acts as the filter; equivalently a fixed 'expert' check rather than a trained reward/value model. The paper explicitly states it uses a fixed expert and does NOT train a separate value function (contrast with full Expert Iteration / AlphaZero-style value nets). No self-as-judge, no learned reward model, no separate retrospective model.
distillation_target: model-weights. Each outer iteration distills the set of answer-correct (and rationalization-repaired) reasoning chains back into the base model's weights via fine-tuning; the reusable artifact is the improved reasoner itself, not an external memory, skill library, prompt, or constitution.
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered (algorithmically engineered self-training loop), not RL-emergent in the R1 'aha' sense. The bootstrapping loop, the answer-correctness filter, and especially the rationalization repair step are hand-designed scaffolding around standard fine-tuning. However, the resulting capability (a model that learns to produce better, sometimes-novel rationales by training on its own successful reasoning) is an emergent product of the loop; the paper's human eval found STaR rationales preferred 30% more often than few-shot rationales (p=.039) and 74% more often than human-written rationales (p<.001).
memory_type: skill-library is NOT used; closest is none / cumulative-training-set. There is no external memory module. The only 'persistence' is the accumulating fine-tuning dataset of correct rationales used to retrain weights each iteration, plus the fixed few-shot prompt set used during sampling.
memory_persistence: cross-task within the training distribution: the learned reasoning skill is baked into weights and transfers across all problems in the dataset and to held-out test problems (and, for arithmetic, to out-of-distribution 9-10 digit sums never seen in training). There is no per-episode scratchpad retained across inference calls; persistence is at the parameter level, not an episodic store.
memory_curation_mechanism: self-summarized/curated via correctness-filtering and re-training from scratch. Curation = keep only reasoning chains whose final answer matches ground truth (line 5 filter), augmented with rationalization-generated chains for failures; the fine-tuning dataset grows across iterations (e.g., CQA final model trained on 78.2% via rationale generation + 8.5% via rationalization). Each iteration RE-TRAINS the original pretrained model on the accumulated set rather than continuing the prior checkpoint, which prevents compounding drift; few-shot prompting during sampling is reported to reduce rationale 'drift' away from the seed rationale style.
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level. The corrective signal is the binary correctness of the final answer only; there is NO step-level, token-level, or block-level credit assignment within a rationale. A wrong final answer discards the entire rationale's gradient (the indicator reward zeroes it out); rationalization then regenerates a whole new chain conditioned on the correct answer. The paper notes a confound: in high-chance settings (e.g., 5-way CQA ~20% random, binary tasks) correct answers can come from bad reasoning, which outcome-level filtering cannot catch.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task. STaR learns transferable reasoning ability by training on successful chains across the whole dataset; the improvement generalizes to held-out test problems and even out-of-distribution arithmetic lengths. It is not an intra-task within-one-instance refinement loop (contrast Self-Refine); it is a dataset-level, weight-update self-improvement loop.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision via rationalization (recover from a failed attempt by reasoning backward from the provided correct answer, then training as if the model produced that chain unaided), which is a form of avoidance for future episodes (the repaired chain teaches the model to solve similar problems next time). It is NOT mid-trajectory in-flight recovery; correction happens between attempts/iterations, not during a single rollout.
task_domains: math (symbolic arithmetic and grade-school word-problem math) and QA/reasoning (commonsense multiple-choice QA). Specifically: n-digit integer addition (symbolic/arithmetic), CommonsenseQA (commonsense reasoning), and GSM8K (grade-school math word problems). No code, web-navigation, embodied, or dialogue domains in this paper.
benchmarks: Arithmetic (n-digit summation, dataset built following Nye et al. 2021 'Show Your Work' scratchpads), CommonsenseQA (CQA; Talmor et al. 2019, 5-way multiple choice), and GSM8K (Cobbe et al. 2021; 7,473 train / 1,319 test grade-school math word problems requiring 2-8 calculation steps).
headline_result: On CommonsenseQA, STaR with rationalization reaches 72.5% dev accuracy with a 6B GPT-J base, vs 60.0% for GPT-J fine-tuned to directly predict answers (+12.5 absolute) and comparable to a 30x larger GPT-3 (175B) direct-finetuned baseline at 73.0%. On GSM8K, STaR with rationalization reaches 10.7% test accuracy vs 5.8% for GPT-J direct-finetuned (+4.9 absolute, ~1.8x) and 3.1% few-shot CoT GPT-J. On 2-digit arithmetic, accuracy jumps from <1% to 32% after one fine-tuning iteration with rationalization.
baselines: Few-shot Direct GPT-J (no rationale), Few-shot CoT GPT-J (with rationale), Few-shot CoT LaMDA 137B (Wei et al. 2022 chain-of-thought), GPT-J fine-tuned to directly predict the answer ('GPT-J Direct Finetuned', trained on 100% of data), and GPT-3 (175B) fine-tuned to directly predict the answer (Xu et al. 2021, for CQA). STaR-without-rationalization vs STaR-with-rationalization is the internal ablation.
gains_vs_baseline: CQA: STaR-with-rationalization 72.5% vs strongest comparable same-size baseline GPT-J Direct Finetuned 60.0% = +12.5 absolute, using only 86.7% of training data; STaR-without-rationalization = 68.8% (+8.8). STaR (72.5%) approaches the 30x larger GPT-3 at 73.0%. GSM8K: STaR-with-rationalization 10.7% vs GPT-J Direct Finetuned 5.8% = +4.9 absolute (~1.84x), using only 28.7% of training data; STaR-without-rationalization 10.1% (rationalization gives little extra on GSM8K). Arithmetic: rationalization enables learning many digit-lengths at once (2-digit <1% -> 32% in one iteration) and OOD generalization to 9-10 digits unseen in training. Few-shot prompts during fine-tuning add ~+8 on CQA (60.9->68.8 without rationalization; 69.9->72.5 with).
compute_cost_profile: Training-dominated: an iterated SFT loop with full-dataset rationale sampling per outer iteration plus repeated fine-tuning from the original checkpoint. Arithmetic ran ~20+ iterations; GSM8K capped at the 30th iteration after 7,912 cumulative training steps (36 iterations for STaR-without-rationalization plus 10 more with rationalization). Training starts at ~40 steps in iter 1 and grows ~20% per outer loop (arithmetic variant: 300 steps then +20/iter). All on a single TPU-v3 node, batch 8 x len 1024, Adam, lr 1e-6. Inference is single-pass greedy (low temperature) — STaR explicitly REJECTS high-temperature multi-sampling as an alternative to rationalization because generating 10 samples is ~10x slower and degrades reasoning quality; rationalization is the cheaper data-expansion mechanism.
known_limitations: (1) Cold-start floor: the base model's few-shot performance must be above chance for iteration 1 to bootstrap — GPT-2 could not bootstrap even on arithmetic; the initial model must be large enough to have some reasoning ability. (2) High-chance/low-answer-cardinality settings (e.g., binary decisions, 5-way MC) yield many correct-answer-but-bad-reasoning chains; outcome-only filtering cannot screen these out (an open filtering problem). (3) Requires ground-truth answers for the (large) unlabeled-rationale dataset; the hint-construction for rationalization 'does not follow immediately from the question and answer' and may be nontrivial in some domains. (4) Re-training from scratch each iteration is expensive and the gradient-signal effects are hard to measure. (5) Faithfulness: the model can reach correct answers via flawed reasoning / logical fallacies (documented CQA failure patterns: question-implies-answer, individual-vs-general statements), and on GSM8K sometimes 'accidentally' answers correctly with fewer/skipped steps.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: oracle-label/ground-truth. STaR fundamentally depends on access to the correct final answer for every training problem: it both filters generated rationales by answer-correctness AND uses the gold answer as the hint for rationalization. This is the discriminating variable — STaR's self-improvement is gated on ground-truth answer labels (not on intrinsic self-verification). The authors note self-consistency majority-vote (Wang et al. 2022) could relax this to question-only data, but that is future work and yields lower performance (later shown by Huang et al. 2022 LMSI).
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive but requires-oracle. With ground-truth answer labels, the loop reliably and substantially improves reasoning across all three tasks; rationalization further accelerates and improves learning (decisive on arithmetic, modest on GSM8K, ~+3.7 on CQA over no-rationalization). It is NOT an intrinsic self-correction method — improvement is contingent on the answer-correctness oracle; without labels the method as-presented does not apply.
calibration_effect: not-measured. The paper predates the reasoning-model calibration / 'reasoning tax' lens and reports no confidence-calibration metrics. It does discuss a related pathology: low-temperature sampling makes correct-without-rationalization examples the ones the model is 'most confident' in, giving a weaker gradient signal — but this is a training-signal observation, not a calibration measurement.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a. STaR is a self-improvement training method, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis system; it does not classify failure modes, attribute a responsible agent, or perform counterfactual step localization. It only uses coarse outcome-correctness to filter data (it does, qualitatively, catalog CQA reasoning failure patterns in an appendix, but does not localize or attribute errors algorithmically).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets the data-bottleneck failure of reasoning models (no rationale-annotated data and weak few-shot reasoning) and the 'no training signal from failed problems' failure of naive self-training (which rationalization fixes by injecting backward-derived chains for hard/failed problems). In MAST-style terms it most relates to mitigating under-exploration / failure-to-solve-hard-problems and, via rationalization, avoiding the self-training plateau; conversely it can entrench 'superficial reasoning' (correct answer, unfaithful chain) because filtering is outcome-only.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new reusable benchmark/dataset of failure traces is released; STaR uses existing datasets (CommonsenseQA, GSM8K) and a generated arithmetic dataset (following Nye et al. 2021). The contribution released is the method and code (https://github.com/ezelikman/STaR), not a labeled failure-trace corpus.
builds_on: Chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022); scratchpads / 'Show Your Work' (Nye et al. 2021); explanation-based commonsense QA and rationalization seed idea (Rajani et al. 2019 'Explain Yourself!'); few-shot in-context learning (Brown et al. 2020 GPT-3); finetuned instruction following (Wei et al. 2022 FLAN); Expert Iteration / ExIt (Anthony et al. 2017) and its formal-math use (Polu et al. 2022) as the iterated-learning/self-play inspiration; policy-gradient / PPO framing (Schulman et al. 2017); self-consistency (Wang et al. 2022) as a discussed extension; GPT-J 6B base (Wang/Mesh-Transformer-JAX 2021).
extended_by_or_inspired: Directly seeds the rejection-sampling / self-training-for-reasoning lineage: LMSI / Huang et al. 2022 (self-improve with majority-vote pseudo-labels), RFT rejection fine-tuning (Yuan et al. 2023), ReST (Gulcehre et al. 2023) and ReST-EM (Singh et al. 2023, EM-style RL fine-tuning), V-STaR (Hosseini et al. 2024, trains a DPO verifier on correct+incorrect STaR traces for best-of-N), Quiet-STaR (Zelikman et al. 2024, token-level latent thoughts), TRICE (Hoffman et al. 2024, marginal-likelihood over multiple traces), Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization (Pang et al. 2024), B-STaR (Zeng et al. 2025, exploration/exploitation balance + PRM), Lean-STaR (Lin et al. 2025, theorem proving), AdaSTaR (2025, adaptive data sampling / FLOPs reduction), CARE-STaR (2025, constraint-aware), process-supervision (Uesato et al. 2022). Widely cited as the ancestor of RL'd self-improvement of reasoning (precursor framing for o1/R1-style training).
citation_count: ~909 (Semantic Scholar, paperId 23dd78e424d32f6a48660dcd67ce994b8a7db8be / CorpusID:247762790, as of June 2026).
reasoning_model_native: no (predates). STaR uses a 6B GPT-J base and predates o1/R1-style models with built-in/RL-emergent reflection. However, it is widely regarded as the conceptual ancestor of the train-on-your-own-correct-reasoning paradigm underlying modern reasoning models; Quiet-STaR (same lead author) is a closer step toward native always-on reasoning.
on_policy_distillation_link: strong / foundational. STaR is essentially self-distillation: the model generates rollouts and is fine-tuned (distilled) on its own answer-correct traces. The authors explicitly frame it as approximating a policy-gradient objective with greedy (low-variance) decoding and multiple gradient steps per batch (PPO-like reuse); rationalization is framed as an OFF-policy estimate (sampling from a hint-augmented proposal distribution p(r|x,y) instead of on-policy p(r|x)). It is a canonical predecessor to on-policy distillation / RL fine-tuning of reasoners (ReST-EM makes the EM/RL view explicit).
sample_efficiency: Data-efficient relative to direct-answer fine-tuning: STaR matches/beats baselines while training on a fraction of available labels (CQA: STaR-without-rationalization uses 69.7% and with-rationalization 86.7% of train; GSM8K: 25.0% without and 28.7% with rationalization vs 100% for direct-finetune baselines). Iteration count is the cost axis: arithmetic improves within 1 iteration on 2-digit (with rationalization), full runs ~20-36 iterations; GSM8K capped at 30 iterations / 7,912 steps. Rationalization markedly improves per-iteration sample efficiency on structured tasks (learning multiple digit-lengths simultaneously instead of stage-wise).
